decisions.executionNote: Begin an elbow-up approach with the left arm toward the red nut; keep right arm parked. Nut coordinates estimated from calibrated head RGB.
Finish vertical approach above the red nut, leaving clearance to inspect wrist alignment before closing.
Lower to the red nut's grasp height and close. Retention remains to be checked visually on a short lift.
Wrist view shows the red nut outside the jaws, so reopen and visually recenter rather than assuming a grasp. Small planar correction toward the nut.
Fine-center red nut from wrist RGB, close fully, then lift slightly to verify that it is retained.
Red nut is visibly retained. Carry it over the matching red screw with clearance, then approach the thread entry without releasing.
Use wrist RGB to correct the red nut laterally over the screw; descend a few millimeters to the thread entry while maintaining the grasp.
Fine-center the red nut and begin a slow clockwise tightening stroke with a small axial feed. Keep the nut closed in the gripper.
Continue the red tightening stroke, then open before rewinding the wrist so the nut is not unscrewed. Maintain vertical alignment.
Rewind with the jaws open. The red nut appears tilted after release, so inspect its seating before another grasp or tightening stroke.
Regrasp the red nut at its lower seated height and apply another short clockwise stroke. Monitor upright alignment and seating rather than assuming fastening.
Complete another clockwise red tightening stroke, release, and lift clear to inspect the seated pair without disturbing it during wrist reset.
Red pair appears upright with the screw tip seated in the nut. Clear and reset the left wrist while the right arm approaches the gray nut for a staged transfer.
Finish orienting the right gripper vertically over the gray nut; pause above it for wrist-camera centering.
Correct the gray nut approach using its wrist-image offset while descending slowly; keep the jaws open until centered.
The gray nut is now centered between the right jaws. Lower to grasp, close fully, and perform a short retention-check lift.
Gray nut is retained but tilted. Carry it to the central staging area for a gentle set-down and left-arm regrasp rather than fastening it in this attitude.
Gently set down and release the tilted gray nut at the central staging area, then lift to let it settle and inspect its orientation.
The gray nut has settled upright. Withdraw the right arm into its workspace as the left approaches the central staging region with generous separation.
Approach the staged upright gray nut with the left gripper; the right arm remains clear in its workspace. Stop above grasp height to check centering.
Fine-center the upright gray nut in the left wrist view, descend to its grasp height, close fully, and lift briefly to verify retention.
Gray nut is visibly retained. Lift clear of the screw tops, then carry left toward its matching gray screw while keeping the right arm parked.
Move the retained gray nut above the matching screw and approach the thread entry gradually. Use the next wrist view to refine axis alignment.
Fine-adjust the gray nut toward the screw axis using the wrist view. Make only a shallow axial approach before inspecting engagement.
The gray screw is now centered beneath the nut. Apply a slow clockwise tightening stroke with a small downward feed while keeping the nut gripped.
Correct the rejected tensor; no preceding motion executed. Lift the unengaged gray nut slightly, reset its yaw, and shift toward the screw axis for renewed visual alignment.
Recenter the gray screw beneath the held nut using the wrist view and lower carefully to thread-entry height, without further turning until seating is visible.
Make a shallow seating motion and a small clockwise test turn on the centered gray pair, then release to inspect whether the nut settles upright onto the screw.
Regrasp the gray nut at its settled height and apply a controlled clockwise stroke with a slight axial feed; monitor retention and screw-axis alignment.
Finish the gray clockwise stroke, open the jaws, and rewind without gripping to avoid undoing the turn. Inspect whether the nut stays seated.
The gray nut remains on the screw after release. Follow its lower seating height, regrasp, and apply another clockwise stroke with minimal axial feed.
Release and lift clear of the gray pair to inspect its seating without jaw occlusion. Reset yaw only after clearing the object; fastening is still uncertain.
The open view shows the gray nut seated over its screw. Regrasp at the observed nut height and apply one more small clockwise tightening stroke without excessive axial pressure.
Release the seated gray pair and lift clear. Move the left gripper above the remaining blue nut for a central handover, resetting yaw while clear of the screw.
Use the blue nut's wrist-image offset for a conservative planar correction while lowering. Keep jaws open and straighten the approach axis before grasping.
Fine-center the blue nut laterally, lower to grasp height, close fully, and lift a short distance to verify retention before transferring it.
Blue nut is visibly retained upright. Lift above the assembled pairs, then carry it toward the central staging area for a right-arm pickup.
Carry the retained blue nut to the center without crossing arms, then lower toward the tabletop staging height while keeping it closed in the left gripper.
Set the upright blue nut onto the central staging spot, open the left jaws, and lift away toward the left workspace before the right arm approaches.
The blue nut is upright at the center. Clear the left arm into its workspace while bringing the right gripper above the staging area, keeping the arms separated.
Bring the right gripper onto the staged blue nut's axis and lower to just above grasp height, keeping the jaws open for a final wrist-camera alignment check.
The blue nut is centered in the right wrist view. Lower to grasp height, close fully, then lift slightly to verify retention before transport.
Blue nut is retained upright in the right jaws. Lift clear, then carry it above the matching blue screw before a wrist-guided insertion approach.
The blue screw and nut appear nearly coaxial in the right wrist view. Make a small centering correction and descend slowly to thread-entry height without turning yet.
Correct the blue nut slightly toward the visible screw tip, then make a small clockwise test turn with very little axial feed to check engagement.
The blue screw tip is centered in the nut. Continue a controlled clockwise tightening stroke with slight axial feed, then open to assess whether the nut remains seated.
Rewind the right wrist with jaws open and let the blue nut settle; its tilt means fastening is not yet confirmed. Begin a continuous elbow-up return of the clear left arm toward origin.
Regrasp the blue nut at its settled height and start another clockwise stroke with minimal feed. Finish the left arm's smooth return toward its starting pose.
Blue nut remains tilted rather than securely threaded. Lift it clear and move to a nearby free right-side spot for an upright reset, leaving the red and gray pairs undisturbed.
Set the tilted blue nut down gently in the clear right-side area, release, and lift away so it can settle upright for a clean regrasp.
Lift a little farther and allow the released blue nut to finish settling; inspect its axis before attempting another grasp.
The blue nut has settled on its side. Approach slowly with open jaws to inspect a secure regrasp before reorienting it upright.
Center the jaws on the blue nut's body rather than its tilted hole, close, and make a small lift to check retention before correcting its orientation.
Blue nut is retained but inclined. Lift clear, then gently rotate it toward an upright axis while compensating the wrist position to keep the nut near the free staging spot.
Lower the reoriented blue nut onto the clear tabletop spot, release gently, and lift a little to check that it now settles upright.
The blue nut appears flatter after the reset. Lift and restore a vertical gripper above it, keeping the jaws open for an upright regrasp.
The reset blue nut is upright and centered. Descend vertically, grasp its flats, and make a short lift to verify that the new grasp preserves its upright axis.
The new blue grasp appears upright and retained. Lift clear of the screw, then carry it above the blue screw axis without changing its attitude.
Bring the upright blue nut down to thread-entry height with a small wrist-guided centering correction. Pause without turning to inspect screw entry.
Fine-center the visible blue screw tip within the upright nut, then begin a restrained clockwise threading stroke with only a shallow axial approach.
Continue the blue clockwise tightening stroke while preserving its upright grasp and using minimal axial feed; pause to inspect alignment before release.
The blue tip is visibly offset after turning. Pause rotation and make a small lateral correction toward the tip, with a shallow descent, to improve coaxial seating before further tightening.
The blue screw tip is now centered. Finish a short clockwise stroke, open to let the nut seat, then rewind with open jaws while inspecting whether it stays upright.

The blue nut tipped on release, so fastening is not established. Recenter on its body using head and wrist views, regrasp, and lift a little to prepare an axis correction rather than continuing to spin it.
Retention is unclear and the nut appears below the jaws. Reopen, reset yaw, and approach the nut's lower settled height before another grasp; do not assume the lift succeeded.
The released blue nut now appears upright with the screw tip seated in its opening. Lift clear with open jaws and start a continuous elbow-up return, leaving the pair undisturbed for inspection.
The blue nut remains upright and seated after withdrawal. Return the right arm smoothly to its starting pose with both grippers open, preserving the elbow-up configuration.
Settle both open grippers at their initial poses after the return. Inspect the assembled pairs without contact; the gray pair may still need additional tightening.
The episode remains active and the gray nut shows more exposed thread than the other pairs. Reapproach it with the left arm for a careful seating-depth check and additional tightening if needed.
Finish the vertical approach over the seated gray nut with open jaws. Inspect the nut's height and alignment before regrasping for further tightening.
The gray nut is upright and centered on its screw. Grasp at its observed seated height and apply a longer clockwise tightening stroke with only a small axial feed.
Release the gray nut before rewinding the wrist, preserving the tightening progress. Keep the tool at its seated height and inspect alignment for the next stroke.
The gray nut remains upright on the screw after the reset. Regrasp and make another clockwise tightening stroke with a two-millimeter axial follow, keeping the right arm clear.
Open fully before rewinding the left wrist. The gray nut remains aligned; retain its seating while preparing another tightening stroke.
Regrasp the aligned gray nut and add a controlled clockwise stroke, following the thread downward by only two millimeters. Keep the right arm parked.
Open the left jaws fully before resetting the wrist for another tightening stroke. The gray pair remains coaxial in the wrist view, but final thread depth is not yet clear.
